description: This case study is the report on the grid disturbances of 30 and 31 July 2012 in India, submitted on 8 August 2012 in compliance with an order of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, running to 129 pages. The executive summary explains that a failed monsoon left the Northern Region drawing large amounts of power from the Western and Eastern grids while rain reduced demand in the west, stressing the system, and describes the blackout of all eight northern states at 02:33 on 30 July with a frequency of 49.68 Hz beforehand, the survival of small pockets, and restoration by hydro self-start, with 40% of the load back by 10:00 and full restoration by 16:00. It then covers the second disturbance at 13:00 on 31 July that affected the Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern grids, with about 73,000 MW of demand in the synchronous grid. Access: free PDF download from the regulator's website; no licence is stated. Coverage is the Indian synchronous grid regions. Caveats: only the executive summary was read, and the root causes and recommendations sections were not summarised. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of large interconnected grids, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
